rows.subtopic: Being left out of a party
rows.description: Everyone was invited to a birthday except me and I heard about it later. It hurts a lot. I let myself feel it, tell someone, and do something nice for myself. It may be about numbers, not me.
My stomach drops when I think the teacher will find out I broke the rule. Fear makes me want to hide it, but owning up early usually costs less than being caught lying later.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, guilt, loyalty, pride, resentment, respect

rows.description: I keep replaying what I did, and it feels heavy. Guilt is useful when it leads me to say sorry and fix things, and unhelpful when it makes me sit alone with it for days.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, loyalty, pride, resentment, respect

rows.description: The rule seems silly and I feel angry at the teacher for enforcing it. A wiser move is to ask why the rule exists, or politely suggest a change, instead of quietly breaking it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty, pride, respect
related mind states: playfulness, anger, resentment

rows.description: When I admit a mistake, the teacher stays calm and talks about what to do next. I feel relieved, and I learn that being honest earns trust even when I have done wrong.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty, pride, resentment
related mind states: admiration, relief, calm, trust

rows.description: My friend broke the rule and I want to cover for him. Real loyalty means urging him to own up and standing beside him, not lying so nobody gets in trouble.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, pride, resentment, respect

rows.description: I feel superior because I never break rules, and I look down on those who do. Following rules matters, but scorn makes me lonely; kindness and firmness can sit together.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, loyalty, pride, resentment, respect

rows.description: I enjoy being trusted to watch others, and it feels grand. A good monitor stays fair to friends and strangers alike and remembers that power is a duty, not a chance to boss.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty, resentment, respect
related mind states: anger, pride, trust

rows.description: Classmates call me a tale-bearer because I told the teacher about something harmful. I feel hurt and left out, yet speaking up about real danger is still right; I can seek a trusted adult for support.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty, pride, respect
related mind states: anger, resentment, trust, hurt

rows.description: I am blamed for something I did not do, and my chest burns. It is fair to feel angry; a mature step is to calmly say what really happened later, not shout or sulk.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, guilt, humiliation, trust
